text: The pipeline begins with an input medical scan, such as an abdominal CT image.
The input image passes through a downsampler to prepare it for transformer processing.
Features are processed through the frozen transformer backbone blocks of the pre-trained image encoder.
Trainable LoRA bypass layers enable parameter-efficient adaptation specifically tailored for medical imagery.
The adapted encoder outputs rich image embeddings to guide the hierarchical decoding process.
In stage one, a transformer decoder applies self-attention and cross-attention over default prompt embeddings and image features.
Concurrently, the first-stage pixel decoder upsamples intermediate feature representations.
Outputs from the first-stage transformer and pixel decoders are combined via dot product.
This generates an initial low-resolution probabilistic segmentation map that serves as a spatial prior.
The Class-Balanced Mask-Guided Self-Attention block incorporates this prior to tackle severe class imbalance in medical targets.
This produces enhanced image embeddings that amplify features for tail categories.
The second-stage transformer decoder applies learnable mask cross-attention, spatially modulated by the prior probabilistic map.
Simultaneously, a hierarchical pixel decoder integrates skip connections from stage one to capture intricate local details.
The refined object queries and hierarchical spatial features are multiplied together.
This produces the final high-resolution, prompt-free multi-organ segmentation prediction.
